method_card.title: Daily Routine and Healthy Living
method_card.content:
This lesson covers reflexive verbs for your daily routine and obligation structures for talking about healthy habits. You need to know levantarse and other reflexive verbs, plus three ways to express obligation: deber, tener que, and hay que.

SpanishEnglish
levantarseto get up
acostarseto go to bed
despertarseto wake up
lavarseto wash (oneself)
cepillarse los dientesto brush one's teeth
vestirseto get dressed
descansarto rest
la saludhealth
sano/ahealthy
en formafit, in shape
una dieta equilibradaa balanced diet
deber + infinitivemust / should
tener que + infinitiveto have to
deberíaI should (conditional)
hay que + infinitive (Higher)one must / it is necessary to

Grammar focus — reflexive verbs: Reflexive verbs need a reflexive pronoun before the verb. Me levanto a las siete (I get up at seven). The pronoun changes with the subject: me, te, se, nos, os, se. Never drop the pronoun: levanto is wrong; me levanto is correct.

Grammar focus — obligation: Three structures all require the infinitive that follows: Debo comer mejor (I must eat better), Tengo que dormir más (I have to sleep more), Hay que hacer ejercicio (One must exercise). A common error is writing a conjugated verb instead of the infinitive: *debo como is wrong — the correct form is debo comer.

Model: Me levanto a las siete y me ducho. Para mantenerse en forma, hay que comer una dieta equilibrada y hacer ejercicio. Debería dormir ocho horas cada noche. (I get up at seven and have a shower. To keep fit, one must eat a balanced diet and exercise. I should sleep eight hours every night.)

method_card.title: Food, Drink and Meals
method_card.content:
This lesson covers food and drink vocabulary, mealtimes, expressing preferences with gustar-type verbs, and using the preterite tense to say what you ate.

SpanishEnglish
el desayunobreakfast
la comida / el almuerzolunch
la cenadinner
la meriendaafternoon snack
la manzanaapple
el pollochicken
el pescadofish
el arrozrice
las patatas fritaschips
la ensaladasalad
el quesocheese
me encantaI love (singular thing)
me gustaríaI would like
delicioso/adelicious
sabroso/a (Higher)tasty (Higher synonym for rico)

Grammar focus — gustar agreement: The verb gustar (and encantar) agrees with the thing liked, not the person. Use me gusta before a singular noun and me gustan before a plural noun. Me gusta el arroz (I like rice — singular), me gustan las patatas fritas (I like chips — plural). Spanish also requires the definite article: me gusta el queso, not me gusta queso.

Grammar focus — preterite: Use the preterite to say what you ate or drank. Regular -er/-ir preterite yo endings: comí, bebí, cené. Context words like ayer (yesterday) and anoche (last night) signal the preterite.

Model: Me encanta la paella porque es muy sabrosa. Para el desayuno como tostadas con mantequilla. Ayer cené pollo con arroz y estaba delicioso. (I love paella because it is very tasty. For breakfast I eat toast with butter. Yesterday I had chicken with rice for dinner and it was delicious.)

method_card.title: Physical Wellbeing — Body, Illness and Health
method_card.content:
This lesson covers body parts, describing symptoms with doler, common illnesses, and giving health advice. A key setting for this topic is the doctor's surgery — one of the prescribed transactional settings in the speaking exam.

SpanishEnglish
la cabezahead
el estómagostomach
la gargantathroat
el brazoarm
la piernaleg
la espaldaback
me duelemy ... hurts (singular)
me duelenmy ... hurt (plural)
tengo fiebreI have a fever
tengo tosI have a cough
estoy enfermo/aI am ill
un resfriadoa cold
la gripethe flu
el medicamentomedicine
hay que + infinitiveone must / it is necessary to

Grammar focus — doler: Doler works like gustar: use me duele + singular body part, me duelen + plural body part. The verb agrees with the body part, not the person. Me duele la garganta (My throat hurts), me duelen los pies (My feet hurt).

Grammar focus — tener for health: Spanish uses tener for conditions where English uses 'to be': tengo fiebre (I have a fever), tengo tos (I have a cough). Use estar for general illness: estoy enfermo/a (I am ill — temporary state, so estar not ser).

Model: Me duele la garganta y tengo fiebre. Estoy muy cansado. Hay que tomar medicamentos y descansar en casa. (My throat hurts and I have a fever. I am very tired. One must take medicine and rest at home.)

method_card.title: Mental Wellbeing and Healthy Living
method_card.content:
This lesson (Higher tier) covers vocabulary for emotions, stress, sleep and mental balance. You will use estar + adjective for all feelings, the reflexive verb sentirse, and the present subjunctive after impersonal expressions.

SpanishEnglish
el bienestarwellbeing
el estrésstress
la ansiedadanxiety
sentirseto feel (reflexive)
estar estresado/ato be stressed
estar cansado/ato be tired
estar contento/ato be happy
el equilibriobalance
el sueño / dormirsleep / to sleep
relajarseto relax
el consejero escolar / la consejera escolarschool counsellor
es importante que + subjunctiveit is important that...
es necesario que + subjunctiveit is necessary that...
florecer (Higher)to flourish / to thrive

Grammar focus — estar for emotions: Emotions and feelings ALWAYS use estar, never ser. Estoy estresado (I am stressed — temporary state), está contenta (she is happy). Writing soy estresado is a serious error — stress is not a permanent identity.

Grammar focus — present subjunctive after impersonal expressions (Higher): After es importante que and es necesario que, use the present subjunctive. Regular -ar verbs: drop the -o of the yo form and add -e endings (hablar → hable, hablen). Regular -er/-ir verbs: add -a endings (comer → coma; dormir → duerma). Example: Es importante que duermas bien (It is important that you sleep well).

Model: A veces me siento estresado porque tengo muchos exámenes. Es importante que haya un buen equilibrio entre el estudio y el descanso. Si me siento agobiado, hablo con el consejero escolar porque siempre me ayuda. (Sometimes I feel stressed because I have lots of exams. It is important that there is a good balance between study and rest. If I feel overwhelmed, I talk to the school counsellor because they always help me.)

method_card.title: Sport and Staying Active
method_card.content:
This lesson covers sport vocabulary, the difference between jugar a and hacer, frequency expressions, and using the preterite and imperfect to talk about sport habits past and present.

SpanishEnglish
el fútbolfootball
el baloncestobasketball
el tenistennis
la nataciónswimming
el ciclismocycling
correrto run
ir al gimnasioto go to the gym
mantenerse en formato keep fit
es bueno para la saludit is good for health
dos veces a la semanatwice a week
todos los díasevery day
los fines de semanaat weekends
el atletismoathletics
la equitaciónhorse riding
reduce el estrés (Higher)it reduces stress

Grammar focus — jugar a vs hacer: Use jugar a for ball/team sports: juego al fútbol, juega al tenis. Note the contraction a + el = al. Use hacer for individual activities: hago natación, hace atletismo. Jugar is stem-changing (u→ue) in the present tense: juego, juegas, juega, jugamos, jugáis, juegan. Hacer is irregular in yo only: hago.

Grammar focus — imperfect vs preterite: Use the imperfect for habitual past actions: Cuando era joven, jugaba al rugby todos los fines de semana (When I was young, I used to play rugby every weekend). Use the preterite for a specific completed event: Ayer jugué al tenis con mi hermano (Yesterday I played tennis with my brother).

Model: Juego al fútbol dos veces a la semana porque es divertido y me mantiene en forma. Cuando era pequeño, hacía natación. Ayer corrí cinco kilómetros en el parque. (I play football twice a week because it is fun and keeps me fit. When I was young, I used to go swimming. Yesterday I ran five kilometres in the park.)
